_comment: Rebuilt 2026-09-11 as SIX frames, all looping. reference.png is the master: the piece is now just the travel, he sleeps throughout, and the whole thing cycles. Fewer frames is higher fidelity here -- 6 frames at 256 colours costs less than 15 at 128, so the export can afford roughly half the colour error.
generated: f1 only. f2-f6 are built in post -- a generator cannot close a loop, because the configuration has to repeat exactly and it gives a new arrangement every time.

motion.far_landscape: STATIC. Castle, beacon, viaduct, river, hills. Distant things do not parallax, so holding them is honest, not a cheat.
motion.near_treeline: SCROLLS left, one full tree-spacing over 6 frames. This is what says "travelling" -- close things move, far things do not.
motion.watchers: a conveyor along the ridge: identical motionless figures, evenly spaced, drifting past with the near ground. One exits as the next enters, so it loops -- and it means there are many of them, all down the road.
motion.birds: a wing cycle across the 6 frames plus drift, so they actually fly rather than slide.
motion.flames: beacon and lantern gutter on a 2-frame cycle -- a different period from the birds and trees, so the loop reads longer than 6 frames.
motion.gleam: crimson interior gleam pulses gently; carving glow breathes.

readout.visible: ALL six frames. Every frame is now a lit valley, so the sky behind the text is bright throughout -- which is the condition the reference ink was drawn for.
readout.ink: reference.png rgb(26,12,27), deepened for a 7px face
readout.numbers: stamped at render time -- they change daily
